question.problem:
Given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are two continuous vector-valued functions for which $f(-7)=⟨6,0,-2⟩$ and $g(-7)=⟨2,-1,0⟩,$ determine

$$
{lim}_{t\to -7}[\frac{f(t)}{2}+3g(t)].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple and the addition rule for limits, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to -7}[\frac{f(t)}{2}+3g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to -7}\frac{f(t)}{2}+{lim}_{t\to -7}3g(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{t\to -7}f(t)+3{lim}_{t\to -7}g(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the fact that both functions are continuous, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{t\to -7}f(t)+3{lim}_{t\to -7}g(t) & =\frac{1}{2}f(-7)+3g(-7) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨6,0,-2⟩+3⟨2,-1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨3,0,-1⟩+⟨6,-3,0⟩ \\  & =⟨9,-3,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$
